towns.name: Granville County

reporting.basis: Actual results (Annual Financial Information Report, as published by the Census Bureau)
reporting.scope: All county funds, including the public school system and utilities
reporting.politicalScope: County candidates: commissioners, sheriff, register of deeds and school board

ledger.description: Utility, transit and ABC store charges
Interest, rents, sale of property, special assessments and other

sources.label: U.S. Census Bureau, 2024 Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances, individual unit file (the county's Annual Financial Information Report)
NC State Board of Elections, receipts of Granville County's local candidates since 2023

notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2024, from the Annual Financial Information Report the county files with the Local Government Commission, as published by the Census Bureau. Not a budget.

Includes the public school system, which the county funds and the Census counts as part of the county, shown as schools and left out of the services and overhead shares, as in Connecticut, Massachusetts and Virginia.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities and ABC liquor stores. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Payments to other governments ($1,213,000) are left out, because the government receiving them reports that spending.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.

Political money counts contributions from PACs, unions and other organizations to candidates for county commissioner, sheriff, register of deeds and the county school board, filed with the State Board of Elections since 2023 (none were found). North Carolina bans corporate contributions. Individuals and party and candidate committees are not counted. Committees are placed by office and filing address, so a few may be assigned to a neighbouring county.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

towns.name: City of Creedmoor

reporting.basis: Actual results (Annual Financial Information Report, as published by the Census Bureau)
reporting.scope: All municipal funds, including utilities; schools are run by the county

ledger.description: Utility, transit and ABC store charges
Interest, rents, sale of property, special assessments and other

sources.label: U.S. Census Bureau, 2022 Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances, individual unit file (the municipality's Annual Financial Information Report)
NC State Board of Elections, receipts of City of Creedmoor's local candidates since 2023

notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2022, from the Annual Financial Information Report the municipality files with the Local Government Commission, as published by the Census Bureau. Not a budget.
The Census surveys every government only in Census of Governments years (2022) and a sample in other years, so FY 2022 is the latest available.
Granville County runs the schools and most social services, and residents pay both the city and the county.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities and ABC liquor stores. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Payments to other governments ($25,000) are left out, because the government receiving them reports that spending.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.

Political money counts contributions from PACs, unions and other organizations to candidates for city council (or board of commissioners or aldermen) and mayor, filed with the State Board of Elections since 2023 (none were found). North Carolina bans corporate contributions. Individuals and party and candidate committees are not counted. Committees are placed by office and filing address, so a few may be assigned to a neighbouring municipality.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.
